diagnostic_cards.title: HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA seems blocking for small transfer (2 bytes)
diagnostic_cards.symptom_summary: HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA behaves like a blocking function when transmitting a very small amount of data (for example 2 bytes).
diagnostic_cards.affected_context: STM32H7 SPI with DMA where transfer completion callback is not observed or HAL SPI state remains BUSY for the next transfer.
likely_causes: Very small DMA transfers can expose completion timing assumptions and appear blocking from application perspective
HAL completion callback path is not reached in the tested flow
SPI state is not returned to READY after transfer completion in the observed sequence
Project uses a HAL version or integration path where behavior differs from reference example
confirmed_facts: A documented H7 issue reports HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA completion callback not reached and state stuck BUSY in user scenario
ST response indicates the official example can behave correctly under expected wiring and setup
The symptom is highly configuration-dependent and must be validated on exact board and firmware version
plausible_diagnosis: Application observes blocking behavior because callback completion path is not reached
State machine remains BUSY so next DMA call fails or waits, which is perceived as blocking
Small payload (2 bytes) increases visibility of sequencing or timing defects
debug_checks: Log entry and exit timestamps around HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA call and completion callback
Verify HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback, HAL_SPI_RxCpltCallback, and HAL_SPI_TxRxCpltCallback are linked and hit
Check hspi State transitions READY -> BUSY -> READY on each transfer
Compare behavior with official SPI_FullDuplex_ComDMA reference on same board family
Validate SPI wiring, clock polarity/phase, and DMA stream/channel configuration
possible_workarounds: For tiny payloads, test interrupt mode or polling mode to isolate DMA completion path
Batch small payloads when possible to reduce tiny-transfer edge effects
Pin exact Cube/HAL version known to behave correctly in your project
constraints_or_limits: No universal fix can be asserted without exact MCU board firmware version and wiring context
Issue thread includes conflicting evidence between user report and reference example

diagnostic_cards.st_ready_text: Problem: HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA behaves as a blocking function when transmitting a small amount of data (for example 2 bytes). | Context: STM32H7 SPI with DMA, completion callback not observed or state remains BUSY after transfer. | Symptoms: tiny transfer appears blocking, completion callback not reached, next transfer fails or waits due to BUSY state. | Likely causes: completion path mismatch, state transition issue, version-dependent HAL behavior, configuration-sensitive tiny-transfer timing. | Confirmed facts: issue #115 reports stuck BUSY and callback path concerns; reference example can still work under expected setup; behavior depends on board and integration details. | Debug actions: instrument callbacks and state transitions, validate DMA and SPI wiring/config, compare with SPI_FullDuplex_ComDMA reference, test alternate mode for tiny payloads. | Workaround: use IT or polling for tiny payloads, batch small frames, pin known-good HAL version. | Constraints: requires exact board firmware and wiring confirmation for reliable closure. | Evidence links: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/issues/115 and https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/issues/47 | Keywords: HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA blocking function small amount of data 2 bytes HAL_SPI_STATE_BUSY callback not reached
